extracted.intended_audience: researchers, institutions, and program leaders seeking philanthropic research funding from Schmidt Sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Schmidt Sciences' funding approach: thematic centers (AI, Astrophysics, Biosciences, Climate, Science Systems), programmatic open calls (RFPs/virtual institutes), and procedural rules about how to apply. Clarifies that funding is solicited via targeted calls rather than unsolicited proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: "We proactively seek out grant opportunities and do not accept unsolicited proposals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not submit unsolicited proposals; engagement and applications occur via the foundation's proactively posted open calls/RFPs. If you want funding, monitor the listed open calls and apply through those channels rather than cold-submitting proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply via current open calls / RFPs
rubrics_metrics.description: "Please find our current open calls listed below." (page lists specific 2026 RFPs and other opportunities such as virtual institutes and Research Frontiers Network calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding opportunities are issued as discrete open calls (e.g., '2026 AI for Actionable Matter Modeling', '2026 Science of Trustworthy AI RFP', 'Humanities and AI Virtual Institute (HAVI)'). Interested applicants must apply to those specific calls using the provided 'Apply' mechanisms; review the individual RFPs for eligibility, scope, and application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic funding centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Schmidt Sciences funds work organized in five centers: AI & Advanced Computing; Astrophysics & Space; Biosciences; Climate; Science Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and projects should align with one of these centers. Project topics, methods, and goals should map to the mission and priorities of the relevant center (for example, AI research for the AI center; carbon-cycle or climate-focused work for Climate). Check the center pages or relevant RFP for more specific topical focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support spans basic science to urgent planetary problems
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our team supports researchers pursuing hypotheses that address everything from basic-science questions to pressing problems facing the planet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences funds both fundamental research and applied work with real-world impact. Proposals that clearly articulate a hypothesis addressing important scientific questions or pressing planetary challenges are within scope; emphasize the significance and potential impact in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic, tailored support by hypothesis/challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: "Within each of our five centers, we organize scientific support through programs and projects—tailored to the needs of each specific hypothesis or challenge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is organized programmatically rather than one-off awards; expected fit is to specific program goals and stated hypotheses. Applicants should demonstrate clear alignment to the program's stated challenge and how the project’s design is tailored to that hypothesis or problem. Expect program-level selection criteria and possibly multi-investigator or institutional program structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valued project characteristics: bold science and continuous collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prominent site messaging: "Bold science, deep and continuous collaborations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences signals a preference for ambitious, high-impact research conducted through sustained collaborative efforts. Proposals that are incremental, narrowly scoped, or one-off small projects are less likely to match this preference. Emphasize long-term collaboration plans, interdisciplinary teams, and transformative goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicative funding scale and mechanisms (from news/grantee list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Site news highlights significant awards (examples include multi-million-dollar grants and cohort/fellowship programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past awards and program types (cohorts, virtual institutes, multi-million-dollar project awards) indicate that the foundation funds large-scale, multi-investigator efforts as well as fellowships and institute-style projects. Applicants should consult specific RFPs for award sizes and program structure; design proposals consistent with the scale and collaborative expectations implied by recent grants.
